results.title: Game Dev Tycoon Review - Gamecritics.com
results.content:
I'll admit, some of what takes place in Tycoon does reflect reality to a degree. The brief reviews could be indicative of the industry's obsession with scores as opposed to constructive criticism, and achieving perfect scores and pandering to demographics is all that seems to matter in the game and the real world. However, I don't really think Tycoon really wants to be more than ‘a glimpse' at video game production, and any attempt to comment on the industry from this dull, monotonous experience fails to hit its mark.

"I've played better." Rating:3 out of 10.

Disclosures: This game was obtained via publisher and reviewed on the PC. Approximately 9 hours of play were devoted to the single-player mode, and the game was not completed. There are no multiplayer modes. [...] Newest

I enjoyed reading this review because it explains both the strengths and the weaknesses of Game Dev Tycoon instead of simply praising or criticizing it. I agree that the game is addictive and satisfying when your studio grows, but the feedback system can sometimes feel too vague, making it difficult to understand why one game succeeds while another fails. Even with those flaws, it is still an enjoyable management game that encourages experimentation and makes you appreciate the challenges of running a game development studio. Great review!

# Game Dev Tycoon Review

Tweet Share Share

By Tayo Stalnaker on  in Reviews

## Falls A Bit Short

HIGH The satisfying "ding" that sounds when a game is complete.

LOW A game getting perfect review scores but barely selling.

WTF I haven't updated my physics engine since the 90s and I'm still turning a profit.

Ever have the desire to be a game developer? How about a yearning to understand the development process and discover what it takes to make it (or break it) in the industry? If so, don't play Game Dev Tycoon to find out.

Inspired by the video game management sim Game Dev Story, Tycoon aims to illustrate the inner workings of game design by giving players a trip down memory lane.
